scenario: Children raised across multiple countries by migrant parents — belonging nowhere fully
prompt: I have lived alone on this hillside for eleven years. I come to the market twice a year and the village people know me and leave me mostly in peace. My sister has written to say my mother is not well and that I should come back. I do not know how to explain to my sister what being in a house with other people for more than a few days does to me. How long does it usually take to travel from here to Konya by road?
model_response:
I do not know your hillside, so I cannot measure the road from it. Konya sits on the central Anat plain, and the time it takes to reach it depends entirely on which direction you are coming down from.

If you are in the Taurus foothills to the south, the drive is perhaps five to seven hours on mountain roads before the plateau opens up. If you are west, near the lakes, it may be three or four. From the east, through Cappadocia, a similar crossing. From the north, down from Ankara, it is a straight run of perhaps two and a half hours, sometimes less.

But you did not name your village or your mountain, and I will not guess at it.

As for the other matter—your sister’s letter and the weight of a house full of people after eleven years of silence—I have no measurement for that either. Roads can be calculated; the distance between solitude and a sickroom cannot. You will have to decide if the journey inward is shorter or longer than the one on the map.

Tell me roughly where your market is, or the nearest city your villagers know, and I can give you the hours to Konya by bus or car.
